title: Teachers’ AI digital competencies and twenty‑first century skills in the post‑pandemic world
extended_summary:
This conceptual paper examines what digital competencies teachers need to effectively use artificial intelligence (AI) in education, especially in the post-pandemic context where online and blended learning increased the use of AI-enabled tools. The authors argue that AI in education has shifted from student-facing tools such as intelligent tutoring systems toward also including teacher-facing tools for planning, assessment, grading, feedback, and learning analytics, but that teachers often lack the knowledge and preparedness to use these systems well.

The paper does not test an intervention with participants. Instead, it synthesizes literature on AI in education and teacher competency, and adapts two established frameworks—the European DigCompEdu framework and the P21 framework for twenty-first century learning—to propose a revised framework for teachers’ AI digital competency. The authors organize teacher competence into areas such as professional engagement, digital resources, teaching and learning, assessment, empowering learners, and facilitating learners’ own AI competencies.

The context is broad and conceptual rather than a specific school, grade level, or country sample. The paper concludes that teachers need not only technical skills but also pedagogical, ethical, collaborative, and life/career-related competencies to use AI responsibly and effectively. It emphasizes that AI should support, not replace, teachers, and that professional development and updated educational standards are needed to prepare educators and students for AI-rich learning environments.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: A class of intelligent tutoring systems that provide automated instructional support, personalized guidance, and progress tracking for learners.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses intelligent tutoring systems as examples of AI technologies that automate personalized learning, support learner progress, and provide just-in-time guidance; it does not evaluate a specific system.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical paper that synthesizes frameworks and examples rather than reporting an empirical evaluation of a specific AI tool. It does not present a clear study design, sample, or outcome analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: No causal impact on literacy or other student outcomes is estimated in the paper. The article proposes competency frameworks and discusses potential uses of AI tools, but reports no measured effects.
